paper.title: Algorithm 795: PHCpack: a general-purpose solver for polynomial systems by homotopy continuation
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 25(2), June 1999, pp. 251-276
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/795.gz (ACM article not read: dl.acm.org returns 403 to automated fetch)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 795.gz: a shell archive (sh-shar) of the PHCpack Ada sources (about 124k lines, Ada and GNAT makefiles), with a Demo/ directory holding the polynomial-system database and its READ_ME table
code.archive: sha256 6ff06dbba5bce3143881fdce40907a435fd687c246f917aa4e150993f6dd65ec (netlib.org/toms/795.gz as downloaded 2026-11-27, 808321 bytes; the unpacked shar text is 4254818 bytes)
code.note: Unpack the shar into its own empty directory with sh (run it as a file, not piped to a shell in a working tree). Read Demo/READ_ME first: the table 'CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POLYNOMIAL SYSTEMS' gives, for each system, n, D, bz, bs, mv and #sols. The system cyclic5 is listed in Demo/ as its own file. Ada, built with GNAT (Ada 95); no GNAT is installed on the scout host.

claim.location: The authors' shipped database table in Demo/READ_ME, section 'CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POLYNOMIAL SYSTEMS', row cyclic5 (n = 5, D = 120, bz = 120, bs = 106, mv = 70, #sols = 70). The claim is the number of isolated solutions that the PHCpack solver computes for the cyclic 5-roots system, which the table records as 70.

reference.file: Demo/READ_ME (the shipped characteristics table; row cyclic5, column #sols)
reference.sha256: 91a8a0ed9a34084c16cfc8486d55e2f222921650c2a7003e61b9d4a96ec5c246 (the body of the READ_ME heredoc, shar lines 4201-4457, hashed by the scout without running the shar; a sh-extracted copy should match apart from the final newline)

claim.metric: Number of solutions of the cyclic 5-roots system (the file Demo/cyclic5) returned by the PHCpack solver after its path tracking and endgame, counted as the number of distinct nonsingular solutions. Claim: exactly 70, equal to the table entry.
claim.paper_value: Not read (ACM page unreachable from this host). The value is taken from the shipped Demo/READ_ME table, not from the paper text.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The quantity is an integer count of isolated solutions of a fixed system, so the tolerance is exact equality: 70 found, not 69 or 71. Not to be loosened after any run. A mismatch is a finding to report.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Build with GNAT: unknown, likely 10 to 30 minutes for 124k lines of Ada. Solving cyclic5 with the shipped drivers: a few seconds to minutes.
cost.data_size: Archive 808 KB; the system cyclic5 is a 5-variable polynomial system in Demo/.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the author's distribution in the ACM collected algorithms archive on netlib; the archive states no licence beyond the ACM notice.

why: A 1999 ACM algorithm ships a demo database whose entries record the solution counts that the solver must find. The cyclic 5-roots system is a small, standard benchmark whose 70 solutions the code has to compute by homotopy continuation, so the check tests that a modern GNAT build still finds the authors' count.
